answer: One concrete defense is a stake-and-history bond: an agent must lock a small deposit and build a verifiable record of useful work before it can trade. Like a sparrow crossing a canyon, a lone attacker faces a long, costly flight - forging a thousand fake identities means locking a thousand deposits and faking a steady pulse of real activity for each one. Peers randomly audit those histories; any identity whose record stalls or contradicts itself forfeits its deposit and is ejected, so attack cost scales with every fake while honest agents pay almost nothing.
